Goal: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from the limitation group 'Leakage-free generalisation protocol': L1, L2, L11, L20, L22, L27, L37, C2): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and with a simple supervised baseline trained on the same labelled images (L31) where relevant.

TITLE: MIL-to-mask self-distillation with cross-level agreement
SUMMARY: First train the segmentation adapters with the problem's top-k MIL, then convert their multi-level maps on abnormal source images into pseudo-masks (patches anomalous at three or more levels) and retrain with MVFA's Dice and Focal losses on those pseudo-masks.
HYPOTHESIS: One round of MIL-to-mask self-distillation increases held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over MIL alone, and cross-level agreement (>= 3 levels) yields pseudo-masks with at least 1.5x the precision of deepest-level pseudo-masks.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: segmentation supervision (true masks; top-k MIL only; MIL followed by one or two rounds of pseudo-mask self-distillation). Round 0: top-k MIL (k = 1%) on all source images. Pseudo-mask of an abnormal source image: patches in the image-wise top 5% at >= 3 of the 4 levels, upsampled with nearest neighbour; normal images get empty masks; pixels of abnormal images outside the pseudo-mask but above the image median are ignored in the Focal term. Rounds 1-2: Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities; pseudo-mask precision and recall against true masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC source images (analysis only).
RATIONALE: MIL supervises only the top patches and gives fragmented maps, but its maps on abnormal source images contain coarse localisation. Turning the MIL-trained maps into pseudo-masks with cross-level agreement and training the segmentation adapters on them with MVFA's own Dice and Focal losses (self-distillation) can densify the supervision while still never using an expert mask.
METHOD: 1) Round 0 as in the problem statement (loss.py: topk_mil). 2) New script make_pseudo_masks.py: run the round-0 seg branch on all source training images, compute per-level probability maps, apply the agreement rule, save masks and ignore maps as .npy. 3) dataset/medical_zero.py: load pseudo-masks for every source dataset (seg_idx >= 0 for all six). 4) train_zero.py round 1: existing Focal + Dice with an ignore weight map. 5) Optional round 2 regenerates pseudo-masks from the round-1 model. Hyper-parameters: top 5%, agreement >= 3 levels, released learning rate and epochs per round.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL only. Ablations: agreement threshold (2, 3, 4 levels); top percentage (2%, 5%, 10%); number of rounds. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over MIL only.

TITLE: DINOv2-affinity propagation of MIL evidence into pseudo-masks
SUMMARY: Refine the MIL-trained patch maps of abnormal source images by propagation over a frozen DINOv2 patch-affinity graph and use the result as pseudo-masks for MVFA's Dice and Focal losses.
HYPOTHESIS: DINOv2-refined pseudo-masks increase held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over the unrefined MIL maps and over CLIP-affinity propagation, while image AUROC changes by less than 1 point.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: pseudo-mask refinement (none; DINOv2 affinity propagation; CLIP-feature affinity propagation). Stage 1: top-k MIL (problem statement). Stage 2: for each abnormal source image, DINOv2 ViT-S/14 patch features on a grid matched to MVFA's, affinity A_ij = max(0, cos)^8, row-normalised; m' = (0.7 A + 0.3 I)^3 m; pseudo-mask = m' > 0.5 max(m'). Stage 3: Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask IoU (analysis), pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: Image-level MIL localises a handful of the most anomalous patches. DINO features are spatially coherent, so a random walk over a DINO patch-affinity graph can grow MIL evidence into region-shaped pseudo-masks that supervise MVFA's segmentation adapters densely, with DINO used only offline during training.
METHOD: 1) Stage 1: loss.py topk_mil in train_zero.py. 2) New script refine_masks.py: torch.hub DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (frozen), patch features resized to MVFA's patch grid, affinity and propagation in torch; save masks. 3) Stage 3: existing Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks for every source image (normal: empty). 4) DINO is not used at test time; inference cost unchanged. 5) Hyper-parameters: alpha 0.7, beta 8, t 3 (ablation alpha {0.5, 0.7, 0.9}, t {1, 3, 5}).
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL only; CLIP-affinity propagation. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over MIL only.
